summary: In this Verge interview, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney reflects on a federal jury siding with Epic against Google, finding illegal monopoly over Android app distribution and in-app payments. He discusses evidence like Project Hug and the Spotify deal, compares the Google and Apple cases, and explains Epic's refusal of special deals. He also covers settlement talks with Sundar Pichai, next steps worldwide, and Epic Games Store plans.
one_line: Epic CEO Tim Sweeney discusses the jury verdict against Google, evidence from the trial, comparisons with Apple, and Epic's next steps.
key_facts: A nine-person federal jury found that Google has an illegal monopoly over Android app distribution and in-app payment systems, and illegally tied Google Play billing to its app store.
Tim Sweeney is Epic's CEO, co-founder and controlling shareholder, and attended almost the entire four-week trial in person, missing one day because of 'non-Epic issues'.
Sweeney said it was the biggest antitrust verdict benefiting everybody against a tech company since US v. Microsoft in the 1990s.

Sweeney said Google's Project Hug offered payoffs to 27 different developers to undermine Epic's store efforts; Activision, Riot and Supercell had direct distribution plans that Google paid them not to pursue.

Under a Spotify deal, Spotify paid 4 percent when using Google's payment service, versus the 30 percent Google forces on other developers; Sweeney called 4 percent a reasonable rate for an unbundled payment system.
Sweeney said Epic has always turned down special deals; his 2019 email to Google executives asked that all developers be allowed to process payments themselves and keep the revenue.
Sweeney said Google employees turned off chat history to get documents destroyed when conversations touched on antitrust issues.
Sweeney said 'Apple was ice and Google was fire', since Google put its deals in writing while Apple's restrictions are internal and absolute; he said Apple deserves at least as harsh scrutiny.
Sweeney said he and Sundar Pichai met for an hour in settlement talks but were 'rather far apart' and reached no settlement.
Sweeney said the verdict covers a worldwide market excluding China, and cited the European DMA and cases coming up in Australia and the UK.
Sweeney said the Epic Games Store has 80 million monthly active users since launching in 2018, versus Steam's 120 million.
An editor's note corrected Sweeney's claim that Fortnite has more concurrent users than Steam: Fortnite hit 7.6 million when Steam had 10.1 million, and Steam generally peaks above 30 million.
Sweeney said there are no hard feelings toward Match Group, which settled, and that Epic expanded to nine times its pre-Fortnite size and now aims to live within its means.
Sweeney said there is no legal linkage between the Google verdict and Epic's appeal in the Apple case.
